La fórmula de la distancia de un punto a: The formula for the distance from a point to a plane is so convenient thanks to Ludwig Otto Hesse, a nineteenth-century German mathematician who proposed writing the equation of the plane divided by the magnitude of its normal. In that Hesse normal form, substituting a point into the equation gives its distance to the plane directly, with a sign: positive on one side and negative on the other. It is the same formula as in this topic, without the absolute value, and it is the one graphics programs use today to know which side of a surface each point falls on.
